title: agent-land.sh: set CARGO_TARGET_DIR per worktree to fix cargo test permission conflicts
description:
When agent-land.sh runs 'cargo test', multiple worktrees share the same target/ directory from the main checkout. Concurrent instances (or even a single worktree when another process holds a lock) get 'Permission denied' writing .rcgu.o files, causing the quality gate to fail.

Fix: write CARGO_TARGET_DIR per-worktree into .agent-env in agent-start.sh, e.g.:
  export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$WORKTREE_ROOT/target

This gives each worktree an isolated build cache and avoids cross-instance write conflicts.
close_reason: Added CARGO_TARGET_DIR per-worktree to agent-start.sh (.agent-env) and agent-land.sh (before cargo test)

title: Adapter: honor fixture _path instead of always writing rename.py
description: jedi test/lsp_compat.py:175 (run_rename) always writes the case code to <tmpdir>/rename.py and ignores the fixture's `_path` kwarg (e.g. `'_path': 'import_tree/pkgx/deep_consumer.py'`). Relative imports in those cases then cannot resolve, so relative-import-from-parent-pkg and relative-import-from-dot fail for reasons unrelated to zuban. RefactoringCase already resolves `_path` (jedi test/refactor.py:49-52). Fix: write the code to that path under the tmpdir, open that URI, and make the diff output's per-file naming and ordering match jedi's expected blocks. Verified 2026-09-13: with the file at its real path, zuban returns the expected edits for relative-import-from-parent-pkg even with empty client capabilities.

comments.author: agent-claude-claudebox-135615
comments.text: Fixed in jedi d9789fd1 (test/lsp_compat.py, local commit on refactoring-test-coverage, not yet pushed): write case code at fixture _path; sort per-file diff blocks by path like Refactoring.get_changed_files. Rename suite vs zuban: 50->52 passed, 15->13 failed; only relative-import-from-dot and relative-import-from-parent-pkg changed.

title: Adapter: declare workspaceEdit client capabilities in LSP initialize
description: jedi test/lsp_compat.py:155 (start_server) sends `capabilities: {}` in initialize. A real editor declares workspace.workspaceEdit support, and zuban refuses any rename that needs a file-rename resource op when that capability is missing: -32803 'Client does not support rename capability.' This alone made the 'module' and 'relative-import-from-dot' cases look like zuban gaps (zuban-b0w, zuban-bz2, both closed as artifacts). Fix: declare `workspace: {workspaceEdit: {documentChanges: true, resourceOperations: ['create', 'rename', 'delete']}}`. Check the adapter's diff builder handles `{kind: 'rename', oldUri, newUri}` entries in documentChanges (it currently only reads entries with textDocument+edits) so it can emit jedi's 'rename from/rename to' header lines. Verified 2026-09-13: with those capabilities, zuban's module rename output matches jedi's expected result.
close_reason: Fixed in jedi a7e00dee (refactoring-test-coverage): lsp_compat.py now declares workspaceEdit documentChanges + create/rename/delete resourceOperations in initialize, and run_rename emits jedi's 'rename from/rename to' headers for {kind: rename} documentChanges entries. 'module' passes in the fixture suite (16 -> 15 failures, no new failures). relative-import-from-dot now gets past -32803 but still needs zuban-ex5 (_path). package-with-stub / weird-package-mix fail on a zuban package-rename bug, filed as zuban-alv (deferred).

title: Adapter: collect all-URI edits and produce per-file diffs for multi-file rename
description: The lsp_compat.py adapter only captures edits for the primary rename.py URI and ignores changes to other files in the workspace edit response. Multi-file rename cases (e.g. 'import', 'module') return edits for several files; the expected output is a sequence of per-file diffs. Fix: iterate over all URIs in documentChanges/changes, apply edits to each file, and produce a combined diff string with one diff block per changed file, ordered to match jedi's expected output (definition file first, then rename.py). Depends on zuban-861 (aux files must exist in workspace first).

title: Adapter: copy fixture aux files to temp workspace for multi-file rename
description: The lsp_compat.py adapter writes only rename.py to a temp dir, but cross-file rename cases (e.g. 'import', 'module', 'in-package-with-stub') need auxiliary files like import_tree/ to exist in the workspace. Without them, zuban cannot resolve imports and the rename either fails or produces no cross-file edits. Fix: copy the jedi refactor fixture directory tree (excluding rename.py itself) into the temp workspace before running each case. The fixture dir is test/refactor/ in the jedi checkout.
close_reason: Implemented in jedi repo: lsp_compat.py now copies fixture aux files (import_tree/ etc.) into the temp workspace so cross-file rename cases can resolve imports. Pushed to jedi/refactoring-test-coverage.

title: agent-start.sh: add Rust, jedi repo, and ZUBAN_TYPESHED setup steps
description: Improve scripts/agent-start.sh to match jedi's script quality: verify/install Rust toolchain, ensure the jedi repo is checked out alongside, set ZUBAN_TYPESHED in .agent-env, and verify the debug binary exists (or run cargo build).
design:
## Steps to add (modelled on jedi's agent-start.sh)

### Rust toolchain check
After bd/jq checks, verify cargo is available:
  if ! command -v cargo &>/dev/null; then
    source ~/.cargo/env 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  if ! command -v cargo &>/dev/null; then
    echo "ERROR: cargo not found. Install Rust from https://rustup.rs" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

### Ensure zuban is built
  if [ ! -f "target/debug/zuban" ]; then
    echo "Building zuban (first run, may take a few minutes)..."
    cargo build
  fi

### Ensure jedi repo is checked out alongside
  JEDI_DIR="$(cd .. && pwd)/jedi"
  if [ ! -d "$JEDI_DIR" ]; then
    echo "Cloning jedi alongside zuban..."
    git clone https://github.com/emclain/jedi "$JEDI_DIR" --branch refactoring-test-coverage
  fi
  if [ ! -d "$JEDI_DIR/.venv" ]; then
    echo "Setting up jedi Python venv..."
    python3 -m venv "$JEDI_DIR/.venv"
    "$JEDI_DIR/.venv/bin/pip" install -q -e "$JEDI_DIR/[testing]"
  fi

### Add ZUBAN_TYPESHED and JEDI_DIR to .agent-env
  cat >> "$worktree/.agent-env" <<ENVEOF
export ZUBAN_TYPESHED=$REPO_ROOT/third_party/typeshed
export JEDI_DIR=$JEDI_DIR
ENVEOF

### Update the final instructions to include test run
  echo "  bash scripts/run_jedi_rename_tests.sh   # run rename tests"

title: Rename: module/file rename not implemented
description: Renaming a module does not produce a file rename operation (rename from/to), only updates the import reference. Jedi produces a file rename plus source edits.
notes:
Deferred: requires changes to core zuban codebase, not test harness. Hold until zuban rename implementation work is prioritized.
2026-09-12 re-review: diagnosis likely STALE, do not act on as written. Filed 2026-03-31T04:23, ~2h45m BEFORE the adapter gained multi-file support (zuban-861/zuban-5f7, closed 07:05); never re-validated afterward. zubanls request_handlers.rs::rename already emits ResourceOp::Rename(RenameFile) via changes.renames(), and that code is unchanged since the fork point. Module rename is notably ABSENT from zuban-bz2's post-fix failure list. Re-measure before any core zuban work.
2026-09-13 re-measured against jedi fixture suite post upstream-sync (579 commits, zero diff in rename path): the 'module' case still fails, and now returns null/error for the whole rename rather than a partial result. The 2026-09-12 'likely stale, re-measure' note does not hold up -- module rename being absent from zuban-bz2's failure list was only because it was never in bz2's scope (import-as-alias/relative-import/nonlocal-rename), not evidence of a fix. Remains open; requires core zuban work (RenameFile support in the module-rename path).
close_reason: Not a zuban gap: test-harness artifact. Re-probed 2026-09-13 with the server driven directly. jedi test/lsp_compat.py:155 sends `capabilities: {}` in initialize, so the client never declares workspace.workspaceEdit.resourceOperations. A module rename needs a RenameFile resource op, and zuban's ensure_valid_workspace_edit (crates/zubanls/src/request_handlers.rs:818) rejects the whole request with -32803 'Client does not support rename capability.' With `workspaceEdit: {documentChanges: true, resourceOperations: [create, rename, delete]}` declared, the 'module' case returns exactly jedi's expected result: text edits in rename.py plus `rename import_tree/some_mod.py -> import_tree/renamedm.py`. Refusing rather than sending text-only edits is defensible (renaming imports without renaming the file would break them), and the maintainer is skeptical of file-rename refactoring anyway (upstream #488). Harness fix tracked in a new adapter bead. Closing.

title: Rename: var-not-found, keyword-param2 return null unexpectedly
description: Two cases return null/error from zuban where a rename result is expected: var-not-found (renaming an undefined variable) and keyword-param2. Needs investigation to determine if these are adapter issues or zuban gaps.
notes:
Deferred: requires changes to core zuban codebase, not test harness. Hold until zuban rename implementation work is prioritized.
2026-09-12 re-review: bundles three unrelated causes and double-counts two. (1) nonlocal-rename rests on an INVALID fixture: jedi test/refactor/rename.py:616 uses 'nonlocal x' against a module-level x, which is a SyntaxError (no binding for nonlocal x found). zuban returning null is arguably correct; jedi is the outlier and the fixture should be retired. (2) keyword-param2 duplicates zuban-0nm. (3) var-not-found is the only case uniquely owned here, and refusing to rename an undefined name is defensible for a type-checker-first tool. Recommend narrowing to var-not-found only, or closing.
2026-09-13: jedi-dbp fixed the invalid fixture (nonlocal x nested inside an enclosing function instead of module scope). Re-ran the LSP comparison with the corrected fixture: nonlocal-rename now PASSES against zuban, confirming the 2026-09-12 hypothesis -- zuban's handling of this rename direction was correct all along; it was only ever rejecting invalid input. Narrows this bead to var-not-found and keyword-param2 (which duplicates zuban-0nm) only.
close_reason: Nothing left that is a zuban bug. Re-probed 2026-09-13. keyword-param2 is the same root cause as zuban-0nm (definition/references don't resolve keyword-argument names), and that bead now carries it. var-not-found: zuban consistently refuses an unresolvable name. prepareRename errors with 'The reference "undefined_var" cannot be resolved', rename errors with 'Could not find the definition', and references returns null. Refusing to rename an undefined name is defensible for a type-checker-first server, so this is not worth reporting upstream. (nonlocal-rename was already resolved via jedi-dbp.) Closing.

title: LSP: definition/references don't work inside string annotations (rename misses forward refs)
description: String annotations used as forward references (e.g. def f(x: 'Foo') -> 'Foo') are not updated when the referenced name is renamed. Jedi recently added this support.
notes:
Deferred: requires changes to core zuban codebase, not test harness. Hold until zuban rename implementation work is prioritized.
2026-09-12 upstream check: NOT fixed upstream. zuban rename implementation is byte-identical between fork point (origin/master 2026-03-30) and upstream/master 2026-09-12 across 579 commits — references_for_rename md5-identical, zero diff lines in the request_handlers.rs rename path. Still real: single-file and adapter-independent.
2026-09-13 root cause: not rename-specific. Inside a string (forward-reference) annotation, textDocument/definition and textDocument/references both return null, and references from the class def return only the def itself. Repro: `class Foo: pass` / `def f(x: "Foo") -> "Foo": return x`, request definition on "Foo" inside the quotes. The type checker does resolve these names: `zuban check` on `def f(x: "Fooo")` reports `Name "Fooo" is not defined [name-defined]`. So the checker understands them but the navigation features don't; rename inherits the gap via the shared ReferencesResolver. Upstream framing: report as 'go-to-definition/references don't work inside string annotations'. Use a class in the repro, not the jedi fixture's `pre = 1` (a variable is not a valid type and would derail the report). No existing upstream issue found (#523 is about the checker misreading string literals as forward refs, unrelated).

title: LSP: definition/references don't resolve keyword-argument names (rename misses kwarg call sites)
description: When renaming a parameter, zuban renames the def site and body but not keyword argument uses at call sites (e.g. f(param=3) → f(lala=3)). Jedi handles this correctly.
notes:
Deferred: requires changes to core zuban codebase, not test harness. Hold until zuban rename implementation work is prioritized.
2026-09-12 upstream check: NOT fixed upstream. zuban rename implementation is byte-identical between fork point (origin/master 2026-03-30) and upstream/master 2026-09-12 across 579 commits — references_for_rename md5-identical, zero diff lines in the request_handlers.rs rename path. Still real: single-file case, so unaffected by the adapter multi-file fix. Best first candidate for actual work — narrowest scope of the remaining gaps.
2026-09-13 root cause: not rename-specific. Probed the server directly (definition/references/hover, not just rename). On a keyword argument at a call site (`param` in `f(param=3)`): textDocument/definition -> null, textDocument/references -> null, and references from the def site omit the call-site kwargs. Hover on the same position DOES resolve it (shows `param1: Any`), so the server already knows the binding. Rename uses the same ReferencesResolver as find-references (crates/zuban_python/src/lib.rs:352; goto.rs find_references_in_file runs goto on every name, and goto_name has no NameParent::Kwarg handling), so fixing definition/references should fix rename for free. keyword-param2 (rename from the call-site kwarg) fails with -32603 'Could not find the definition' for the same reason; that case now lives here (zuban-ljo closed). Upstream framing: report as 'go-to-definition and find-references don't work on keyword arguments', not as a rename gap. Minimal repro: `def f(param): return param` / `f(param=3)`, request definition on the kwarg. No existing upstream issue found (searched zubanls/zuban 2026-09-13).

title: Rename: cross-file edits not returned for definition file
description: When renaming a symbol defined in another file, zuban only returns edits for the importing file, not the file where the symbol is defined. The definition site is left unchanged.
notes:
Deferred: requires changes to core zuban codebase, not test harness. Hold until zuban rename implementation work is prioritized.
2026-09-12 re-review: diagnosis likely STALE, same provenance as zuban-b0w. Filed 2026-03-31T04:23, before the adapter multi-file fix at 07:05; never re-validated. The LSP handler maps every change to its own change.path.as_uri(), so per-file edits across files are structurally supported, and that code is unchanged since the fork point. Re-measure before any core zuban work.
close_reason: Re-measured 2026-09-13 against the jedi fixture suite post upstream-sync (579 commits, no rename-path diff). The 'import' fixture case is exactly this scenario (rename a symbol imported from another file) and now passes, with edits returned for both import_tree/some_mod.py (definition file) and rename.py (usage file). Confirms the 2026-09-12 re-review's 'likely stale' diagnosis: the definition-file edit gap was closed by the adapter's multi-file fix (zuban-861/zuban-5f7), not a zuban regression. Closing.

title: Zuban test harness: launch server and feed jedi fixture cases via adapter
description: Write the harness that builds and launches zuban as a stdio LSP server, integrates with the adapter (zuban-elm), and wires everything into pytest.
design:
## Responsibilities

The adapter (zuban-elm) handles fixture parsing and LSP message translation.
This harness owns everything around the server process:

- Build zuban (cargo build) or locate an existing binary
- Launch zuban as a subprocess with stdio transport
- Pass the server command into the adapter's --lsp-cmd option
- Manage server lifecycle: startup, per-session initialization, shutdown
- Handle server crashes or unexpected exits gracefully (mark affected cases as errors)

## pytest Integration

- conftest.py fixture that builds/locates the zuban binary (session-scoped)
- A session-scoped LspServer fixture that starts zuban once per test file
- --zuban-bin option to skip the build step and point at an existing binary
- --lsp-cmd falls back to the located binary if not explicitly given

## Build Step

  cargo build --bin zuban 2>&1

Cache the binary path in a session-scoped fixture. If the build fails, skip
the entire test session with a clear message rather than failing each test.

## Startup Handshake

After launching the process, complete the LSP initialize/initialized handshake
before running any cases. Fail fast with a useful message if the server does
not respond within a timeout (e.g. 10s).

## Fixture File Scoping

One zuban process per fixture file (matches adapter spec). The harness
should support pytest's parametrize grouping so the server is not restarted
between cases in the same file.

## Out of Scope

- Testing non-rename LSP features
- Multi-workspace or multi-root setups
- Notebook support

title: LSP rename adapter: run jedi fixture-format tests against any LSP server
description: Build a thin pytest adapter that parses jedi's #? fixture format and drives rename operations against a stdio LSP server, enabling cross-server comparison of rename behavior.
design:
## Scope

- Rename only. Other refactoring types (inline, extract, etc.) are out of scope.
- Single-file cases only. Multi-file rename (e.g. the _path kwarg in jedi fixtures) is out of scope.
- No jedi dependency at runtime.

## Inputs

1. A fixture file in jedi's refactor format (e.g. test/refactor/rename.py)
2. A command to launch the LSP server (e.g. \`zuban --stdio\`, \`jedi-language-server\`)

## Case Parsing

Reuse _collect_file_tests from test/refactor.py as-is. Each RefactoringCase gives:
- case._code — the source text (including the #? marker line)
- case._line_nr — 1-indexed line number of the rename target (line after #?)
- case._index — 0-indexed column of the rename target
- case._kwargs['new_name'] — the new name
- case.type — 'diff', 'text', or 'error'
- case.get_desired_result() — the expected output string

## LSP Client

A minimal asyncio stdio client. Messages needed:
- initialize (handshake; request UTF-8 position encoding)
- initialized notification
- textDocument/didOpen
- textDocument/rename
- shutdown + exit

One server process per test file (not per case) to avoid startup overhead.

## Position Mapping

- lsp_line = case._line_nr - 1  (LSP is 0-indexed)
- lsp_character = case._index   (0-indexed in both)
- Negotiate UTF-8 encoding in initialize to avoid UTF-16 offset issues

## Result Comparison

diff cases: apply WorkspaceEdit edits to case._code, produce unified diff with
difflib.unified_diff. Header uses fixture basename (e.g. "--- rename.py").

text cases: apply edits and return full resulting source text.

error cases: pass if server returns LSP error response or null result.
Do not check error message text (messages differ across servers).

## Applying Text Edits

Apply edits end-to-start (by position) to avoid offset drift.

## Interface

  pytest test/test_lsp_rename.py --lsp-cmd="zuban --stdio"

--lsp-cmd is a required option. Cases parametrized with ids like rename-simple.

## Out of Scope

- Error message text comparison
- prepareRename testing
- File renames
- Multi-file cases
- Non-rename refactorings

title: agent-start.sh cannot claim a specific issue id
description: agent-start.sh always claims the highest-priority ready issue. Claiming a named issue (e.g. when the user asks for one) means replicating its fast-forward, claim, worktree, submodule and .agent-env steps by hand, which drifts from the script. Found while landing zuban-by4. Likely fix: accept an optional issue id as $1 and claim only that one.

title: run_jedi_rename_tests.sh uses bare python3, which lacks pytest
description: scripts/run_jedi_rename_tests.sh runs 'python3 -m pytest' from PATH. In this container /usr/bin/python3 has no pytest ('No module named pytest'); only $JEDI_DIR/.venv (which agent-start.sh creates) does, so the script fails unless the venv is activated by hand. Found while working zuban-ex5. Likely fix: prefer $JEDI_DIR/.venv/bin/python when it exists.

title: Adapter: per-case files persist in the shared tmpdir across rename cases
description: jedi test/lsp_compat.py run_rename writes each case's code into one session-wide tmpdir and never removes it. rename.py is overwritten by the next rename.py case, but files written at a fixture _path (import_tree/rel_consumer.py, import_tree/pkgx/deep_consumer.py, since zuban-ex5) stay for the rest of the session, and rename.py keeps the previous case's code during _path cases. A later case renaming a name those files reference would get extra edits that jedi's run (which never writes them to disk) would not. No current case is affected; the full suite gave identical results apart from the two fixed cases. Found while working zuban-ex5.
close_reason: Moved to jedi's tracker as jedi-8cn: the change is in jedi, which zuban agents treat as read-only.

title: zubanls rename: package rename emits malformed file-rename paths
description: Found 2026-09-13 while landing zuban-0nn (adapter now declares workspaceEdit.resourceOperations). Renaming a package gives bad resource ops. package-with-stub (rename pkgx -> renamedp): zuban emits RenameFile import_tree/pkgx/__init__.py -> import_tree/renamedp__init__/.py and __init__.pyi -> import_tree/renamedp__init__/.pyi. The separator lands in the wrong place, and it renames the __init__ files instead of the directory, where jedi expects 'rename from import_tree/pkgx / rename to import_tree/renamedp'. weird-package-mix (pkgx -> rename): no rename op at all, only text edits. Both cases fail in the jedi fixture suite for this reason, independent of the adapter. Adapter note for later: once zuban emits directory renames, jedi's expected diffs use '--- old/path +++ new/path' headers for edited files inside the renamed directory. lsp_compat.py make_diff currently writes the same name on both lines. Requires core zuban changes.

title: jedi fixture import-as-alias expects import-breaking output
description: jedi test/refactor/rename.py 'import-as-alias' (line ~595) renames the local alias `fb` to `alias`. Its expected output also renames `foobar = 3` to `alias = 3` in import_tree/some_mod.py but leaves `from import_tree.some_mod import foobar as alias` in rename.py, which raises ImportError. jedi passes the fixture (verified 2026-09-13), so jedi really produces this broken output. zuban renames only the alias's three occurrences in rename.py, which is the correct result. Same class of problem as the invalid nonlocal fixture fixed in jedi-dbp. Fix belongs in the jedi repo: correct the expected output to the alias-only rename. Optionally also file jedi's cascading rename as a jedi bug.
close_reason: Moved to jedi's tracker as jedi-9no: the change is in jedi, which zuban agents treat as read-only.

title: zuban: missing multi-file edits for import-as-alias, relative-import, nonlocal-rename
description: After the adapter fix (zuban-5f7), these cases still fail because zuban does not return edits for non-primary files: import-as-alias (should rename in some_mod.py), relative-import-from-dot, relative-import-from-parent-pkg. Needs server-side multi-file rename improvements.
notes: 2026-09-12 upstream check: NOT fixed upstream. zuban rename implementation is byte-identical between fork point (origin/master 2026-03-30) and upstream/master 2026-09-12 across 579 commits — references_for_rename md5-identical, zero diff lines in the request_handlers.rs rename path. Most credible of the multi-file beads: filed 07:15, AFTER the adapter multi-file fix landed at 07:05, so its three cases failed against a working adapter.
close_reason: All three cases are harness/fixture artifacts; zuban is correct on each. Re-probed 2026-09-13 with the server driven directly. (1) relative-import-from-dot is a module rename (rel_sibling.py -> renamed_sibling.py), so it hits the same empty-client-capabilities rejection as zuban-b0w; with resourceOperations declared, zuban returns jedi's expected edits plus the file rename. (2) relative-import-from-parent-pkg: lsp_compat.py:175 always writes the case to rename.py at the workspace root and ignores the fixture's `_path` (import_tree/pkgx/deep_consumer.py), so `from ..deep_mod` cannot resolve. With the file at its real path, zuban returns edits in deep_mod.py and deep_consumer.py matching jedi's expected output, even with empty capabilities. (3) import-as-alias: jedi's expected output is broken code. It renames `foobar` to `alias` in some_mod.py but leaves `from import_tree.some_mod import foobar as alias` in rename.py, which raises ImportError (jedi passes this fixture, so jedi really produces it). zuban renames only the local alias (all 3 occurrences in rename.py), which is correct. Follow-ups filed as adapter/fixture beads. Closing.

title: .agent-env is not gitignored; shows untracked in every worktree
description: agent-start.sh writes .agent-env (CLAIMED_ID, BEADS_ACTOR, paths) into each worktree, but neither .gitignore nor info/exclude covers it, so git status shows it as untracked and a 'git add -A' would commit it. Found while landing zuban-by4. Likely fix: add .agent-env to .gitignore.

title: zubanls rename: minor LSP capability-conformance nits
description: Minor LSP-conformance findings from the 2026-09-13 probe. Low value; hold unless reporting something else upstream. (1) rename always builds WorkspaceEdit.documentChanges (crates/zubanls/src/request_handlers.rs:520-522) without checking the client's workspace.workspaceEdit.documentChanges capability, while ensure_valid_workspace_edit (:818) strictly checks resourceOperations. Code actions use the plain `changes` map instead. (2) For module renames, prepareRename reports a valid range even when the following rename is certain to fail the resourceOperations check. The capabilities are known at initialize time. (3) The error text 'Client does not support rename capability.' reads as if the client lacks textDocument/rename, when it means the 'rename' resource-operation kind. Requires core zuban changes.
